Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

couple phrase

a couple of: two or so, a few

also a couple of, one or two, two or three, a few

classical

Cic. Clu. 72: ūnus et alter diēs intercesserat
Hor. Ep. 2.1.74: versus paulō concinnior ūnus et alter (Lewis & Short)

ūnus et alter

phrase: both words agree with the noun

one or two, a couple

Lewis & Short: of an indefinite number, one and another, one or two. Also ūnus alterve: ūnum alterumve diem, a day or two (Cic. Fam. 3.9.2).

Other words

  • paucī, paucae, pauca — a few

    adjective, plural · also used · classical · Catull. 13.1–2: paucīs … diēbus

    A few, without a number.

Examples

  • Ūnus et alter diēs intercesserat

    a day or two had gone byCic. Clu. 72

  • cēnābis bene, mī Fabulle, apud mē paucīs, sī tibi dī favent, diēbus

    you’ll dine well at my house, Fabullus, in a couple of days, if the gods are kind to youCatull. 13.1–2

See also two, couple.

SourcesLewis & Short: unus · Lewis & Short: alter · Lewis & Short: paucus
